newsitem.title: USA: Sparton sets plan to exit auto supply.
newsitem.headline: Sparton sets plan to exit auto supply.

text.p: Sparton Corp said on Thursday that it will exit the automotive supply business.

None of the large automotive original equipment companies including Ford Motor Co, Chrysler Corp and General Motors Corp, is willing to give the company appropriate price adjustments for increases in the costs of materials, labor and overhead, Sparton said in a statement.
Sparton said that even though its automotive sales were increasing and required additional borrowings by the company, profit margins kept getting smaller.
Directors decided there is little chance for a company of its size to become more profitable unless it raised a lot of new capital to expand the business and become much larger, Sparton said.

Earlier, Dura Automotive Systems Inc said it would acquire Sparton Engineered Products Inc-KPI Group for $80.5 million in cash. Part of the proceeds from this sale will be used to pay off all bank loans, Sparton said. The balance will be used to expand the company's electronic contract manufacturing business at five of its plants where it has additional floor space and capacity.

Sparton said its board also authorized the sale of Sparton Engineered Products-Flora Group that makes automotive horns. Discussions are underway with a prospective purchaser for Flora at this time, the company said.
Sparton added that its annual meeting plans have not been finalized and it will advise shareholders of a date and time as soon as it is established.
Sparton makes defense, commercial, industrial and contract electronic systems and products.
Shares of Sparton closed up 5/8 to 8-5/8, a new high.
